source_metadata.title: Gastrointestinal tolerability of once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg in adults with overweight or obesity, and the relationship between gastrointestinal adverse events and weight loss

duplicate_review.finding: No duplicate atom IDs or same-anchor/canonical-statement duplicates detected.

consistency_review.finding: STEP 1-3 pooled adverse-event denominators (2116/1261) differ by one participant per arm from randomized counts (2117/1262); atoms preserve the analysis-specific denominators where available.

extraction_limitations: The publication is a post-hoc pooled analysis of STEP 1-3 plus a separate STEP 4 withdrawal analysis; it is not a newly randomized trial specifically designed around the post-hoc mediation question.
The mediation analysis depends on no-unmeasured-confounding assumptions for post-randomization GI adverse events.
STEP 4 randomized-period tolerability applies to participants who tolerated semaglutide 2.4 mg through the 20-week run-in and therefore is not an unselected initiation population.
The descriptive week-68 weight analysis excludes participants who discontinued treatment before week 68.
schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated mediation-effect context or post-randomization mediator object; mediation effects are represented as quantitative_result atoms with descriptive tags.
The schema has no dedicated sponsor-role or author-employment structure; funding and conflicts are represented as their supported atom kinds with canonical statements.
